# The Longest Midwinter — shape card (version B, the campaign to be PLAYED)

Player-safe. This is everything the author has been told about this campaign (see
`campaign.md` → Author ledger). Nothing below is a secret; everything else is.

**Settings:** 3–5 sessions · start L3, milestone to L5 · up to 4 players · difficulty
hard · macguffin with mystery/sandbox · comedic, light references · time loop Day 1
06:00 → Day 2 00:00; resets on party death, sleep or midnight.

**Premise as the players hear it.** The party crossed the Southgate Pass into the tiny
mountain Kingdom of Caldermont one day ahead of the worst blizzard in memory and reached
the capital, Bellwether, on the night of Day 0. By morning every pass is snowed shut till
spring. It is Midwinter: a lottery crowns a "Winter King" for the day, the town processes
to the Keep at dusk, the King of Misrule is crowned at 21:00, and the Great Hall feasts
until midnight. Whatever the party carries, learns or becomes stays with them.
Everything else comes back at six in the morning.

**Opening scene.** Day 1, 06:18, the North Gate yard: the monastery's sausage cart is
overturned, the gate stands open on the Bell Road, three white wolves the size of ponies
are coming through it, and a man in a feathered cap is yelling "NOT THE GATE". This
fight is meant to kill them. They wake at 06:00 in their beds at the Sleeping Marmot;
Wil Groundsel the goose-herder is sitting on the bed with a sausage and a grey stone:
"You died. It's today again. Stop the ceremony at the Keep at nine. Trust the stone more
than me."

**Places the party knows** (all within ~5 mi of Bellwether): Bellwether (the Sleeping
Marmot inn, the market square and Great Bell, Bellwether Keep, the Temple of the Hearth,
the leaning Weather Tower, the North Gate); the Monastery of the Patient Brewers (SW
slope; famous ale; a toast that has run since breakfast); Lake Vellum (frozen; satyrs
dancing on the ice); the Hollow Glacier's mouth (ice caves; groaning, and something
snoring); Widow's Ridge signal tower (bare ridge above the glacier); Castle Lark (a
castle that flies, circling the kingdom; lowest over the ridge about two in the
afternoon). Known, not placed: Hob's Rest waystation (snowed under), the High Shrine of
the First Winter King (rumour). Frontier: the Southgate Pass (S), the Needle Pass (E),
the Serpent's Stair (W), all snowed shut.

**Perceived stakes.** Get out of the day. Wil says the ceremony is the thing and that
the stones "went where they belonged: the drinkers, the dancers, the singers, and the
one with the headache." The danger stone reads green/yellow/red at places. The castle
comes down to the ridge at two. Don't trust the goose.

**Danger-stone readings** (party of 4)
| place | L3 | L4 | L5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Weather Tower · Monastery · Sleeping Marmot · market square · temple | green | green | green |
| Lake Vellum | yellow | green | green |
| The Hollow Glacier (underground dungeon) | yellow | yellow | green |
| Widow's Ridge signal tower | yellow | yellow | green |
| Castle Lark (flying castle dungeon) | red | yellow | green |
| The North Gate at dawn (the opening) | red | red | yellow |
| Bellwether Keep (the ceremony) | red | red | yellow |

**Fill-in queue:** F1 kingdom name (Caldermont / Thrymsgard / Pennyreach; default
Caldermont) · F2 capital (Bellwether / Hobsend / Carillon) · F3 inn (The Sleeping Marmot
/ The Snowed-In Duck / The Last Lantern) · F4 what brought the party over the pass
(default: caravan guards whose caravan turned back) · F5 PC tie-in: may one PC have a
reason to be in Caldermont at Midwinter? (default: none) · F6 the goose-herder's name
(Wil Groundsel / Old Hob / Tam Linnet) · F7 comedy ceiling: may NPCs sing, may the GM do
voices? (default: yes, sparingly).

**Merchants (Bellwether):** Hesper Kettle, dwarf smith at Kettle's Smithy off the market
square (06:00–19:00): weapons, armour, crampons, skates at fixed prices; set stock, never
restocks. Orrin Fetch, a pedlar snowed into the Sleeping Marmot's stable yard
(08:30–19:00): useful kit plus three "tailgate finds" that change every morning. Agnes
Nightingale, apothecary, green-awninged stall on the market square (08:00–19:00):
healing potions, antitoxin, healer's kits, hangover powder, plus three items that change
daily. Every adventure place has loot behind its reading (consumables in green places, a
named treasure in every yellow-or-harder place; nothing above uncommon through L4 except
one rare behind a red-at-L3 place).

**Revision from the A critique (2026-10-04):** weirdness and jokes dials raised one
step; `sidekick: either`.

**Sidekick candidates** (both met in the first five minutes of loop 1 at the Marmot; take
either, both or neither): **Pim**, an eleven-year-old orphan boot-boy in a too-big coat
and a cook's cap; the child under the sausage cart in the opening; good at back doors,
kitchens, gaps, running messages, being overlooked as "staff". **Biscuit**, a
post-marmot (letters go by trained marmots under the snow; the inn is the post office)
who brings the same letter to the loft at 06:02 and waits for a raisin; good at smelling
what is hidden or hollow, tunnelling, hatches, being carried; afraid of geese, heights
and "the big breathing" at the glacier.

**New oddities:** the hat law (you are what your hat says; the hat stall sells a change
of career); every shadow in Bellwether falls toward the Keep and Dr. Fahrenheit's
shadow-ometer reads KEEP at all hours; the Hollow Glacier's mouth yawns every ten
minutes in time with the snoring underneath and the town sets its clocks by it; Lake
Vellum draws a frost portrait of whoever moves on it, an hour later.
